extracted.intended_audience: education administrators, Title IX coordinators, institutional legal counsel, policymakers, and stakeholders submitting or reviewing Title IX rulemaking comments
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations explaining regulatory changes, legal interpretations, responses to public comments, and procedural guidance on topics such as parental rights, religious exemptions, athletics, employee duties, and grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of transition plan provisions (§§106.2(s), 106.16, 106.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed §§106.16 and 106.17 and the definition in §106.2(s) because those provisions are outdated and describe requirements that are no longer operative or necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions governed transition of certain single-sex institutions to coeducational institutions shortly after the 1975 regulations; removal does not relate to Title IX's coverage of gender identity discrimination. §106.2(s) was removed because the defined term is no longer included in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of athletics adjustment period (§106.41(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed §106.41(d) because the three-year adjustment period required for compliance with the original 1975 athletic regulations has passed and the provision is no longer operative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The removal does not change other provisions governing athletics. Effective date and retroactivity for other amended provisions are addressed elsewhere (Effective Date and Retroactivity, Section VII.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final regulations should provide clarity and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department determined that the greater clarity and specificity of the final regulations will better equip recipients to create and maintain school environments free from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department based revisions on review of prior regulations and extensive public comment; specific clarifying provisions include identifying bases of prohibited sex discrimination (§106.10), articulating employee duties (§106.44), and providing detailed grievance procedures (§§106.45 and 106.46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee duties—reporting to Title IX Coordinator (§106.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees' duties under §106.44 are generally limited to reporting to the recipient's Title IX Coordinator information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes that employee obligations do not exceed what Title IX requires; duties are focused on reporting rather than investigative or disciplinary actions by employees themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Title IX training for employees (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require annual Title IX training for employees so they can adhere to the regulations' requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is intended to help employees identify and report conduct that may constitute sex discrimination and to limit inappropriate or overbroad responses by institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed grievance procedures (§§106.45 and 106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department provided detailed grievance procedures for recipients to follow in addressing complaints under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedures are cited as part of the Department's effort to standardize and strengthen Title IX protections and to ensure recipients have clear processes for addressing sex-based harassment and discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of bases of prohibited sex discrimination (§106.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department has identified bases of prohibited sex discrimination in the regulations (see §106.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion of §106.10 clarifies the sources/bases of discrimination covered by Title IX and is referenced throughout the preamble when addressing specific concerns (e.g., gender identity coverage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of parental rights (§106.6(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.6(g) affirms that the regulations do not derogate legal rights of parents, guardians, or other authorized legal representatives to act on behalf of their minor child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states the regulations do not interfere with parents' rights to raise children, keep them safe, instill moral values, decide curricula, or access education records; it rejects claims that the final regulations diminish parental rights and notes religiously exempt institutions remain an option for parents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of FERPA parental access to education records
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations derogates a parent's FERPA right to review and inspect the education records of their children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies that Title IX regulations do not interfere with established parental rights under FERPA or teacher-parent communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: No regulation of curricula (34 CFR 106.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX regulations explicitly state that nothing in the regulation shall be interpreted as requiring or prohibiting or abridging in any way the use of particular textbooks or curricular materials (34 CFR 106.42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reiterates it does not regulate curricular choices or compel specific instruction; this addresses commenters' concerns about federal overreach into curricular matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: No criminal penalties or vicarious liability for parents
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not impose criminal penalties on parents, do not hold parents vicariously liable for their children's actions, and do not require recipients to investigate or reprimand parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies that concerns about investigations or criminalization of parents are unfounded and that nothing in the regulations creates such obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-campus conduct and interplay with First Amendment (Mahanoy/Tinker)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department states the final regulations do not derogate parental control over off-campus conduct and observes that Mahanoy did not resolve the issue of a recipient's authority to discipline off-campus speech that creates an on-campus sex-based hostile environment; Tinker may apply in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation's scope regarding hostile environment sex-based harassment and off-campus or online speech is addressed in the definition discussion (Section I.C). The Department rejects broad claims that the regulations improperly extend school authority to off-campus conduct without case-specific analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exemption retained (§106.12) and statutory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to amend §106.12; Title IX since 1972 excludes application to educational institutions controlled by a religious organization where application would be inconsistent with the organization's religious tenets (20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Congress included the religious exemption in the statute, elimination of the exemption is a congressional prerogative; the Department's 2020 amendments codified longstanding agency practice regarding the exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.12(c) control criteria and burden to establish exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.12(c), a recipient must establish that it is controlled by a religious organization and show the scope of any claimed exemption; recipients are not entitled to formal deference and bear the burden to establish eligibility for an exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.12(c) provides multiple ways to show control but does not allow 'tenuous relationships' to suffice. The relevant tenets are those of the controlling religious organization, not personal beliefs of officials or employees. Even if an exemption is claimed, OCR may investigate conduct that the tenets do not address, and a recipient may not use an exemption to retaliate.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.12(b) assurance process—pre-assertion and assertion during investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.12(b), a recipient may, but is not required to, submit a written statement to OCR seeking assurance of a religious exemption prior to invoking it, and may also assert an exemption in response to a pending OCR investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes this approach balances administrative burdens and ensures asserted exemptions meet statutory requirements. Receiving an assurance does not always bar subsequent OCR investigation of complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency—OCR religious exemption correspondence subject to FOIA; public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters exchanged with recipients regarding religious exemptions are subject to Freedom of Information Act requirements and, because of repeated requests, OCR posts correspondence regarding assurances of religious exemptions on its website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considers current practice of posting exemption letters or making them available via FOIA responsive to requests for transparency. Prospective students and others may ask recipients whether they rely on any Title IX exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exemption applies to institutions controlled by religious organizations, not individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory religious exemption applies to educational institutions controlled by a religious organization; it does not extend to student organizations, individual employees or students, or institutions not controlled by a religious organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters' requests to extend §106.12 protections to individuals or to student groups in non-controlled institutions were rejected; intersection with First Amendment issues is addressed elsewhere in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR may verify assurances with controlling organization and investigate despite assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: If OCR receives a complaint alleging improper application of a religious exemption or if OCR determines tenets do not address the conduct at issue, OCR may investigate and make a finding; OCR may contact the controlling organization to verify tenets and may decline to recognize an asserted exemption if the organization denies control or interpretation differs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assurance is not an absolute bar to investigation; OCR retains authority to evaluate compliance and the scope of any claimed exemption in context of specific complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate rulemaking for rescinding 34 CFR 75.500(d) and 76.500(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments urged rescinding 34 CFR 75.500(d) and 76.500(d) (prohibiting certain grant recipients from enforcing certain nondiscrimination policies against religious student organizations); the Department did not request comment on these in the NPRM because they are outside this rulemaking and proposed rescission in a separate rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those regulations are addressed in a different rulemaking (see 88 FR 10857, Feb. 22, 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking process and public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department solicited live and written comments (including a June 2021 public hearing and listening sessions) and considered recommendations from practitioners and experts among hundreds of thousands of comments on the July 2022 NPRM; Title IX rulemaking did not require negotiated rulemaking under HEA section 492.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department coordinated with other agencies (OMB) as required by Executive Order 12866. Comments are posted on Regulations.gov and prior stakeholder inputs are discussed in the July 2022 NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department authority to implement Title IX (statutory and judicial bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department relies on statutory authority to implement Title IX (20 U.S.C. 1682) and notes judicial recognition (e.g., Gebser) of the Department's authority to promulgate and enforce requirements effectuating Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This basis underpins the Department's response to commenters who argued the regulations exceeded departmental authority.
